title: What Siri AI means for your email, SMS, and push
summary: Siri AI now searches your customers' email and texts, unsubscribes them by voice, and answers status questions for apps. Here's what changes for senders.
body_markdown:
Siri AI changes what happens to your email, SMS, and push notifications after they're delivered. It reads urgent notifications aloud, searches your customers' Apple Mail and Messages, can delete or unsubscribe from your email when asked, and will soon answer "where's my order?" through apps instead of waiting for your notification. A message used to be done once it was read. Now it's a record Siri can find, act on, and quote back weeks later.


Picture a customer asking Siri, "When does my order arrive?" Siri doesn't open your app. It searches their Mail and Messages and reads back the shipping email you sent on Tuesday. You never record an open, and the email still did its job.


This post covers what happens after delivery. For what happens before (priority notifications, summaries, Mail categories, and text filters), see our[marketer's guide to iOS 27 and priority notifications](https://www.courier.com/blog/ios-27-notifications-marketers) .


## What Siri AI is, and who has it


**Siri AI** is Apple's rebuilt Siri, released September 14, 2026 with iOS 27. It runs on Apple's new foundation models, which Apple says were "custom-built in collaboration with Google and its Gemini models," processing on the device where it can and on Apple's Private Cloud Compute servers when it can't ([Apple Newsroom](https://www.apple.com/newsroom/2026/09/siri-ai-a-profoundly-more-capable-and-personal-assistant-is-here/) ).


Not every customer has it yet:


- It needs an Apple Intelligence iPhone: iPhone 15 Pro, iPhone 15 Pro Max, or iPhone 16 and later.
- It's in beta, available in English, French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish ([Apple Support](https://support.apple.com/guide/iphone/summarize-notifications-reduce-interruptions-iph1fbe7d2b9/ios) ).
- It isn't available in the EU on iPhone at launch, or to users under 13.
- Server-side requests have daily limits, and Apple says "expanded access to such features will be available for a fee in the future."


Here's what it does with the messages you send:


Siri AI capability Status What it means for you


Reads time-sensitive notifications aloud Live (Announce Notifications) Urgent pushes are heard, not seen


Searches Apple Mail and Messages Live since iOS 27 Your emails and texts become searchable records


Deletes all mail from a sender Live since iOS 27 One request clears your history


Unsubscribes from mailing lists iOS 27.3 beta (Nov 3, 2026) Leaving your list takes one sentence


Answers through third-party apps Developer preview, customers in "a few months" Status questions move from your push to Siri


## Siri reads your notifications aloud


This is the one documented way Siri handles your push notifications. With **Announce Notifications** turned on, Siri speaks notifications through AirPods and CarPlay, from apps like Messages and Reminders "and from supported third-party apps." When an app classifies a notification "as time sensitive or as a direct message, Siri plays a tone, then announces the notification automatically" ([Apple Support](https://support.apple.com/en-us/102536) ). Siri doesn't announce while the person is using their phone.


So your most urgent notifications are the ones most likely to be heard rather than seen. A push that depends on an emoji, a visual layout, or a "tap to find out" hook falls apart read aloud. "Your table at Nopa is confirmed for 7:30 tonight" works in any form.


What Apple doesn't document is Siri AI searching or summarizing push notifications after they arrive. The new **Siri Recap** summarizes conversations captured on Apple Watch, not notifications. Until that changes, a push sits in Notification Center until it's cleared, and Siri can't look it up later.


## Siri searches your messages long after you send them


By default, Siri AI searches Apple's own apps, including Mail, Messages, and Notes ([EFF](https://www.eff.org/deeplinks/2026/09/how-limit-what-apples-new-siri-ai-can-access-ios-27) ). In Mail, people can long-press an email and use **Ask Siri** to pull out a tracking number or a flight number ([MacRumors](https://www.macrumors.com/2026/09/23/50-new-things-iphone-can-do-ios-27/) ). Your shipping confirmation from last week is now an answer Siri can give.


Third-party apps work differently. Apple says Siri's personal context extends to them "when developers integrate with Spotlight" ([Apple Newsroom](https://www.apple.com/newsroom/2026/06/apple-introduces-siri-ai-a-profoundly-more-capable-and-personal-assistant/) ). As of November 2026, the third-party apps Apple has named are WhatsApp and Audible, with Microsoft Outlook, Notability, and Tripsy "coming soon." Gmail, Slack, and Microsoft Teams haven't announced support.


That creates a split you can't see from your dashboard. If your customer reads email in Apple Mail, Siri can find your message. If they read it in the Gmail app, Siri can't, at least not yet.


People can limit all of this. Each app has a **Show Content in Search** setting under Settings > Apps > \[app\] > Search, iOS 27.2 added a way to exclude apps from Siri AI, and the **Siri Classic** option in Screen Time turns Siri AI off entirely (EFF).


### What to change


- **Put facts in live text.** Siri can't pull an order number out of an image.
- **Give each message a complete set of facts:** order number, item, date, and status. A message that says "see your account for details" is useless as a search result.
- **Send corrections as new messages.** If a delivery date changes, the old email is still there for Siri to find. A fresh message with the new date gives it something current to read.
- **Keep a durable copy of anything important.** A push covers the moment. Email, SMS, and your in-app inbox keep the record.


That last point is a routing decision. With Courier, one send can deliver the same data to push for the moment and to email and the in-app inbox for the record:


TypeScript


```text
import   Courier  from   "@trycourier/courier"  ;


const   client   = new   Courier  ();  // reads COURIER_API_KEY from the environment


await   client.send. message  ({
message: {
to: { user_id:  "user_8231"   },
template:  "order-shipped"  ,
data: {
orderNumber:  "4821"  ,
item:  "Trail running shoes"  ,
carrier:  "UPS"  ,
trackingNumber:  "1Z999AA10123456784"  ,
arrivesOn:  "Thursday, Nov 13"  ,
},
routing: {
method:  "all"  ,
channels: [ "push"  ,  "email"  ,  "inbox"  ],
},
},
});
```


The push says the order shipped. The email and the inbox entry carry the same order number, tracking number, and date, in text Siri (and your customer) can find later.


## Siri can act on your email, including unsubscribing


In iOS 27, people can ask Siri to act on their mail, including deleting every message from a sender ([9to5Mac](https://9to5mac.com/2026/10/09/heres-everything-new-for-apple-mail-in-ios-27/) ). The iOS 27.3 beta, released November 3, goes further: Siri can now unsubscribe people from mailing lists and undo a message they sent ([MacRumors](https://www.macrumors.com/2026/11/03/ios-27-3-siri-ai/) ). Apple hasn't explained how the unsubscribe works. Apple Mail already shows an Unsubscribe banner on mailing-list mail, so start there when you test it.


Gmail is heading the same way. Its **Manage subscriptions** view lists senders by volume and unsubscribes in one tap, with Gmail sending the request on the user's behalf ([Google](https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/gmail/new-manage-subscriptions-unsubscribe/) ).


Leaving your list now costs your customer one sentence or one tap. That changes the math on volume: every send that isn't worth reading is a chance for someone to say "unsubscribe me from these."


### What to change


- **Offer a middle option.** Let people choose topics, channels, or frequency, or pause for a month. Someone annoyed by daily promos may still want order updates and a weekly digest.
- **Put preferences where people look.** A preference link next to unsubscribe gives people a reason to stay.
- **Make sure your unsubscribe works.** Test your one-click unsubscribe header and process opt-outs quickly, because people now leave through Siri and Gmail without ever visiting your site.


Courier's[preference center](https://www.courier.com/docs/recipients/preferences/overview) handles the middle option: people choose topics and channels, and every send checks those choices before it goes out.


## Siri can answer instead of your notification


On November 3, Apple opened a developer preview that lets "any developer" bring their app's content and actions into Siri AI using **App Intents** ([Apple Developer](https://developer.apple.com/news/?id=gdk2umrf) ). Apple's examples range "from checking a delivery to booking a reservation to placing an order." Siri AI can also surface "any entity in the Spotlight semantic index," and developers can teach it skills that "combine several actions into a single experience." App Store submissions open in spring, and Apple says the feature will reach customers in a few months.


For order and delivery updates, that's a shift from push to pull. Today you send "Out for delivery" and hope it gets seen. Soon, a customer can ask Siri where their package is, and Siri will ask your app directly.


That doesn't make notifications obsolete. Customers won't ask Siri about things they don't know happened, so delays, failed payments, and security alerts still need a push. Routine status, though, increasingly happens on request.


It also creates a consistency problem. If your push says the package arrives Wednesday and your app tells Siri Thursday, the customer hears two answers from one company. Your notifications and your app's Siri answers need to read from the same data.


It isn't a marketing channel, either. No paid placement, ad product, or attribution reporting came with the announcement ([ContentGrip](https://www.contentgrip.com/apple-siri-ai-app-intents/) ).


## Gmail, Slack, and Teams run their own Siri


Apple isn't the only AI reading your messages. The apps your customers use have their own:


- **Gmail** offers free Gemini summaries of email threads for everyone ([Google](https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/gmail/gmail-is-entering-the-gemini-era/) ), and its "High priority only" notification setting lets Gmail decide which emails buzz the phone at all.
- **Slack** added a Today view, Activity triage, and an in-app Focus mode that "silences non-urgent notifications" ([Slack](https://slack.com/blog/news/feature-drop-may2026) ). If your product posts alerts into Slack, they may be read as part of a summary before anyone opens the channel.
- **Microsoft Teams** offers Copilot summaries of chats and threads to people with a Copilot license.


None of these has announced Siri AI integration yet, but the rule is the same across all of them. Literal, specific, self-contained messages hold up under any summarizer. Vague ones get flattened into whatever the model guesses you meant.


## What Siri AI doesn't do yet


A few limits, so you don't plan around features that don't exist:


- Apple doesn't document Siri searching or summarizing push notifications.
- There's no marketer dashboard, paid placement, or attribution for Siri.
- Apple doesn't document whether Siri searches texts in the Messages Unknown Senders filter.
- Nobody has published adoption numbers or engagement data for Siri AI.


## What to do now


1. Write time-sensitive push notifications so they make sense read aloud.
2. Put live text and a complete set of facts in every email and SMS.
3. Give every important push a durable copy in email or your in-app inbox.
4. Send corrections as new messages instead of hoping people find the update.
5. Offer preferences as the alternative to unsubscribing, and keep one-click unsubscribe working.
6. List your most common "where's my X" notifications. They're your first App Intents candidates, and both should read from the same data.
7. Write Slack and Teams bot messages so they survive a summary.
8. Measure actions, because a Siri lookup never registers as an open.


## Wrapping up


Siri AI turns your messages into records. It reads urgent ones aloud, searches the rest weeks later, removes you from an inbox on request, and will soon answer questions your notifications used to answer. The senders who come out ahead are the ones whose messages are clear, complete, and consistent, because those are the messages Siri can use.


For what happens before your customer ever sees your message, read our[marketer's guide to iOS 27 and priority notifications](https://www.courier.com/blog/ios-27-notifications-marketers) .


## Frequently asked questions


### Does Siri AI read push notifications?


Siri reads notifications aloud through AirPods and CarPlay when Announce Notifications is on, and it announces time-sensitive and direct-message notifications automatically. Apple doesn't document Siri AI searching or summarizing push notifications after they arrive.


### Can Siri unsubscribe people from marketing emails?


Yes. The iOS 27.3 beta, released November 3, 2026, lets Siri unsubscribe people from mailing lists in Apple Mail. Since iOS 27, Siri can also delete every email from a sender. Apple hasn't documented how the unsubscribe works.


### Can Siri search Gmail or Outlook?


Not as of November 2026. Siri AI searches Apple's own apps, like Mail and Messages, by default, and reaches third-party apps only when developers integrate with Spotlight. Apple lists Microsoft Outlook as "coming soon," and Gmail hasn't announced support.


### Is Siri AI powered by Gemini?


Apple says its new foundation models were "custom-built in collaboration with Google and its Gemini models." They run on the device and on Apple's Private Cloud Compute servers.


### Can brands pay for placement in Siri AI?


No. Apple hasn't announced any paid placement, ad product, or attribution reporting for Siri AI. Apps can expose actions to Siri through App Intents, which is a product integration, not an ad channel.


### Do Siri lookups count as email opens?


No. When Siri searches Mail and reads back details from your email, no open is recorded. Measure clicks, conversions, and replies instead.
